metadata.title: How far does a learned surrogate of a flowsheet simulator transfer across ores? A closed-circuit, size-by-mineral engine, with cases and ore groups held out
metadata.description:
Learned surrogates of process simulators are often evaluated on random states from plants they have already seen. This technical report compares interpolation, leave-one-case-out, and leave-one-ore-group-out evaluation for five models trained on a steady-state mineral-processing simulator. The simulator tracks mineral mass over 63 size classes, water, closed grinding circuits, and unit-level balance closure. It reports limitations against published examples alongside the comparisons. On a 3,072-state design over twelve authored cases, the multilayer perceptron gives the lowest interpolation recovery RMSE (3.38 percentage points), but has a 26.24-point mean RMSE when each case is held out. The Gaussian process has the lowest mean held-out-case RMSE (10.95 points), while the perceptron has the highest median case-fold R-squared (0.547). Under ore-group holdout, the perceptron's median recovery R-squared is 0.437 across seven groups, but varies from 0.795 for the five chalcopyrite cases to -10.2 for the two gold-in-pyrite cases. Log-upgrade transfer is poor for every model. The cases are authored; these results do not establish performance on operating plants.

The report documents the mineral-processing simulator, its physical models, machine-learning evaluation methods, a process-specific optimization study, data and preprocessing, validation protocols, limitations, and reproducibility. Source code and computational records: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_OreFlow
metadata.version_notes: Expanded research report for OreFlow version 0.10.006, with methods, benchmark results, executable teaching material, and stated limits.
